**Freeze at ~14% context fill — same "thinking stuck" family, with log evidence**

Environment: Windows 11, OpenCode v1.18.18 desktop (local sidecar server), DeepSeek V4 Pro via API, 1M context window, `reasoningEffort: max`.

Symptom: when a session reaches ~14% context fill (~140K input tokens), the chat and permission dialogs freeze (red server indicator). No error in UI, nothing in the log — the stream to `deepseek-v4-pro` goes completely silent (20 min in my last capture), followed by `Aborted` after a manual Esc. No crash, no dumps. It self-recovers after 5–30 min, or after Esc → resend.

What makes this case notable: it reproduces across different sessions at the *same context fill percentage* (~14%), suggesting the stall correlates with accumulated context size, not just long reasoning. Same family as #37609 / #36370 / #38951, but with a measurable trigger threshold.

Workarounds confirmed: Esc → resend succeeds; starting a new session before ~100K tokens prevents the freeze.

Additional real-world confirmation: we encountered this on OpenCode 1.18.10. A single user turn produced 699 assistant messages before it was manually aborted; 649 of those messages had `finish: "stop"` and arrived after the useful response had already completed. This caused substantial unnecessary model API usage.

The behavior is consistent with the ID-ordering termination bug described here, and the `parentID` check in this PR matches the relationship the loop actually needs to establish.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #41964: Desktop sidecar repeatedly crashes with V8 out-of-memory, causing local server red and Failed to fetch — same sidecar OOM crash pattern and `Failed to fetch` symptom
- #38362: OOM crash on startup from event table snapshot / session revert data exceeding V8 heap
- #35088: JavaScript heap OOM after long sessions — no memory budget management

If your crash is specifically triggered by restoring a large binary file tab (rather than general memory growth), this is a distinct root cause and your issue adds useful detail. Otherwise, please check if the above cover your case.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues that report the same underlying `runLoop` exit-condition bug (`lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id` string comparison). Please check:

- #38787: `[Bug] Agent loop produces duplicate responses due to non-monotonic MessageID comparison` — same root cause (ID string comparison not reliably reflecting message order), same `runLoop` exit condition, same suggested fix
- #28618: `runLoop fails to exit when client-generated messageID has clock skew ahead of server` — same broken ID-ordering assumption in `prompt.ts`, same symptom, same suggested fix
- #38801: `message="exiting loop"` — same "exiting loop" symptom traced back to non-monotonic ID comparisons in `runLoop`

The timestamp wrap angle you describe is a distinct root cause for *why* the IDs go out of order, but the broken comparison and the silent-stop symptom are already tracked in those issues. It may be worth adding your analysis there as a comment rather than tracking separately — especially since a fix to the comparison logic in `prompt.ts` would address all three causes at once.

Re-pitching this, because the motivation has become concrete since it was closed as not_planned.

**Concrete demand now exists:** users increasingly expect agent UIs like Tencent's *Marvis* "virtual office" — anthropomorphized multi-agent workspaces with avatars, live status, and task-progress visualization. That entire class of experience is **impossible to build as an OpenCode plugin today**, because the `@opencode-ai/plugin` API is backend-only (hooks / tools / commands) with no way to mount a custom UI surface.

**Feasibility is already proven:** `Nihalmai/opencode-plugin-update` rendered weather cards / charts / forms inline with only a ~3-line core change. The rendering path exists; what's missing is a *supported, external* plugin API.

**A minimal, safe API would unblock a large category of plugins:**
- `registerWebviewPanel(id, url)` → render a sandboxed iframe/WebView in a side panel or settings dialog (lowest risk)
- schema-driven config forms (dropdowns / toggles) rendered natively for plugin settings
- per-agent / per-tool UI components mounted at defined points

This isn't "prompt-engineered UI in chat" — it's letting plugins become first-class UI citizens (dashboards, agent visualizations, native settings) without forking core. As rich agent frontends become table stakes, reconsidering #19919 would unlock a lot of ecosystem value.

Happy to help specify the API or prototype the iframe/webview path.

@mcj777 thanks for the detailed repro — the ~14% context-fill threshold is a great new data point.

This is the same "stuck thinking / silent stream drop" family as #36370, #32366, #38644, #37609, #38951 — but your capture adds something the others lack: a **reproducible trigger threshold** (~14% / ~140K input tokens on a 1M window), which points at accumulated-context-size handling rather than just long-reasoning or a one-off provider error.

Where this issue stays distinct (and worth keeping open alongside those bug reports): the **UX gap** — there's no watchdog, no stall timeout, and no explicit "retry / discard-and-re-ask" affordance when a turn silently hangs. Today the only recovery is a manual `Esc → resend` that throws away reasoning context. A minimal, high-value fix would be:
1. detect a stalled turn (no token / no SSE event for N seconds past the model's typical first-token latency),
2. surface it as a recoverable state with "Retry" / "Discard & re-ask" instead of a silent hang,
3. preserve reasoning context across the retry.

The diagnosis belongs to the bug issues; the watchdog/retry UX is the feature request here. Boosting visibility for both.

### Same bug, native trigger: opencode's own id prefix rolled `f/e/d → 0`

I hit this exact loop, but not from an imported session. My sessions are all native opencode sessions. The id prefix changed on its own.

**What I saw in my local DB (`opencode-stable.db`):**

| id prefix | messages | time span |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `d…` | 4,886 | Apr 20 → May 6 |
| `e…` | 22,891 | May 7 → Jun 25 |
| `f…` | 26,098 | Jun 25 → Aug 14 |
| `0…` | ~1,180 | **Aug 13 →** now |

The old ids grew through the `d…e…f…` range. Then new ids restarted at `0…`, which sorts **before** every `d/e/f` id. So the moment I resume any pre-Aug-13 session and it appends one new `0…` message, the session stops being id-sortable. `runLoop` then treats an old assistant message as the last message, never exits, and the provider returns the 400:

```
This model does not support assistant message prefill.
The conversation must end with a user message.
```

The TUI also renders the session out of order (old block below the new block). `time_created` stays perfectly monotonic the whole time, so the data is fine — only the id-string ordering breaks. This matches your analysis of `runLoop` / `MessageV2.latest()` comparing ids as plain strings; it is just a different way to break the "ids sort chronologically" invariant (an opencode version/id-scheme change, not a third-party importer). It affects native sessions on upgrade, so the blast radius is larger than imported sessions alone.

Fix #1 in the issue (order by `time.created`, id as tiebreak) resolves my case too.

**Workaround while PR #38798 lands**

I wrote a small script that repairs affected sessions in the DB — the data-side mirror of "order by `time.created`". It detects broken sessions (id order ≠ `time_created` order), renumbers each session's messages into `time_created` order (remapping `part.message_id`, `parentID`, `session.revert`), and drops empty errored assistant turns. It makes a full backup first and runs in one transaction with integrity checks.

Script: https://github.com/helgeu/setup/blob/5bfc1ee/nix/bin/opencode-fix-message-ids

```
opencode-fix-message-ids            # detect + list broken sessions (read-only)
opencode-fix-message-ids --all      # fix all
opencode-fix-message-ids -s <id>    # fix one
```

Environment: opencode 1.18.13, macOS arm64, github-copilot `claude-opus-4.8`.

Hit this in production today — sharing field evidence that confirms the report, plus a working recovery procedure for anyone with a bricked session.

## Production timeline (opencode 1.18.10, portable Windows build, UTC+8)

The wrap happened at **2026-08-14 19:19:55 UTC+8** (predicted from the 18:45 ID and confirmed against the 20:28 ID):

| local time | message ID | note |
|---|---|---|
| 18:45:28 | `msg_fffe0770a001…` | pre-wrap, 0xFFFE0770A001 ≈ 0.9976 × 2^48 |
| 20:28:28 | `msg_0003ec4ee001…` | post-wrap |

After 20:28, every prompt in that session logged this and died in ≤105 ms:

```
INFO  loop session.id=ses_… step=0
INFO  "exiting loop" session.id=ses_…
```

No LLM call, no error, no `process`/`stream` log line. New user messages were still persisted to `message` (with `parentID: NULL` — orphaned), so from the UI it looks like "messages sent but nothing ever comes back". Restarting the app does not help.

## Decisive control experiment (rules out network/model)

At 21:13:08 and 21:13:35, same process, same model (`opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro`), 27 s apart:

- bricked session → `loop step=0 → exiting loop` (72 ms)
- fresh session created after the wrap → normal `process → stream → reply`

So this is purely session-local state, exactly as the root-cause analysis predicts.

## Recovery workaround (SQL surgery on opencode.db)

Marking the stuck assistant message `completed` does **not** help — the exit condition is the ID comparison itself. What worked:

1. Back up `opencode.db` (use `sqlite3 .backup` so WAL is included).
2. Rewrite every **pre-wrap** message ID of the affected session to a small, time-ordered sequence that sorts *before* post-wrap IDs, keeping the 12-hex prefix format, e.g. `msg_000000001001…`, `msg_000000002001…`, …
   - update `message.id`, `message.data.id`, `message.data.parentID`
   - update `part.message_id`, `part.data.messageID`
3. Leave post-wrap IDs untouched (they already sort correctly and future IDs will keep growing past them).
4. Restart opencode. The session is responsive again.

## Related

- #38787 (duplicate replies from "non-monotonic MessageID comparison") looks like the *same* wrap manifesting the other way — `lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id` evaluates false-ish ordering so the loop re-processes an old user message instead of skipping the new one. Worth cross-linking.
- Secondary symptom worth noting: users who tried "revert" to rescue a bricked session lost hundreds of messages from view, compounding the data-loss panic. The messages were still in the DB — the revert UI just can't cope with the broken ordering.

Thanks for the precise root-cause write-up — it matches our independent decompilation of the desktop bundle (same `create2` logic, same `runLoop` exit condition).

Thanks for the detailed report. This is intentional behavior for now: when a model omits capabilities, OpenCode applies the catalog defaults, including image input support. Custom providers and models that do not support images should override those defaults by explicitly declaring their input and output capabilities—for example, `input: ["text"]` and `output: ["text"]`. We’re closing this as not planned.

I found a related PR, though it's in a different component:

**Related PR:**
- **#39806** - `fix(session): make message ordering robust to ID wrap`
  - This PR addresses the same ID wrap problem but on the server side for message ordering. PR #42590 is the complementary client-side TUI fix.

No duplicate PRs found

> ## Root cause
> 
> `packages/opencode/src/id/id.ts`:
> ```ts
> let now = BigInt(currentTimestamp) * BigInt(0x1000) + BigInt(counter)
> now = direction === "descending" ? ~now : now
> 
> const timeBytes = Buffer.alloc(6)          // <-- only 48 bits stored
> for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) {
>   timeBytes[i] = Number((now >> BigInt(40 - 8 * i)) & BigInt(0xff))
> }
> 
> return prefix + "_" + timeBytes.toString("hex") + randomBase62(LENGTH - 12)
> ```
> * `now = Date.now() * 0x1000 + counter` needs ~53 bits, but only the low **48
>       bits** are kept. The stored value is effectively
>       `(Date.now() mod 2^36) * 0x1000 + counter`.
> 
> * `2^36 ms = 68,719,476,736 ms ≈ 795.4 days ≈ 2.18 years`. Whenever
>       `Date.now()` crosses an integer multiple of `2^36`, the ID "clock" resets:
>       IDs go from `...ffff...` back to `...0000...`.
> 
> * The first wrap since 1970 that users will hit is `k = 26`, i.e.
>       `26 * 2^36 ms ≈ 1,786,706,395,136 ms` (mid-2026).

The ID format is unchanged in this PR (still wraps every ~795 days), this is tracked in #39806

Additional data point for Windows: **drive-letter case mismatch between the Desktop layout store and the DB hides all sessions in Home**.

## Environment
- OS: Windows 11
- OpenCode Desktop: **1.18.18** (also reproduced on 1.18.7 CLI)
- DB: `C:\Users\<user>\.local\share\opencode\opencode.db`

## Observed
Projects show in Home, but every project renders **zero sessions** — same as the original report. The terminal CLI lists all sessions from the same DB without issue. Clearing the Desktop UI cache (.dat files, Local Storage) did **not** help; "write-touch" via CLI did **not** help either.

## Root cause found
The persisted Desktop layout store (`opencode.global.dat`, key `server.projects`) stores the project worktree with a **lowercase drive letter**:

```
"worktree":"d:\Users\ilsch\Documents\OpenCode\oneS"
```

while the database stores `session.directory` / `project.worktree` with an **uppercase drive letter**:

```
D:/Users/ilsch/Documents/OpenCode/oneS
```

The Home pipeline (`buildHomeSessionRecords` -> `pathKey`) compares `pathKey(session.directory)` against `pathKey(project.worktree)` from the layout store. `pathKey` only normalizes slashes (`\` -> `/`) and does **not** normalize drive-letter case, so on Windows:

```
pathKey("D:/Users/.../oneS") !== pathKey("d:/Users/.../oneS")
```

Every session is filtered out -> "zero sessions" for every project. This matches the symptom exactly and is the same path-sensitivity class as #14570 / #17518, but on the **Home/Desktop layout store** side.

## Workaround (confirmed working)
Align the DB paths to the layout's drive-letter case (lowercase), then fully restart Desktop:

```sql
UPDATE session          SET directory = lower(directory);
UPDATE project          SET worktree  = lower(worktree);
UPDATE project_directory SET directory = lower(directory);
```

Adding a concrete use case where the restart requirement is especially painful: **OpenCode Web with multiple concurrent conversations**.

## Scenario

1. I run OpenCode web (local server) with several conversations open in parallel in the same project/directory — one is a long-running task, others are unrelated.
2. In one conversation I create or update a skill (global `~/.config/opencode/skills/` or project `.opencode/skills/`).
3. I want to use that new/updated skill right away in *another* conversation.
4. There is currently no way to do this without restarting the whole web app — and a restart interrupts every in-flight conversation at once: the running generations are cut off and any partially generated output is lost (session history itself is persisted, so nothing else is lost).

## Why it hurts here specifically

Skills/agents/config are snapshotted **per directory** (`InstanceState` / `ScopedCache`, TTL infinity) and **shared by all sessions in that directory**. So:

- Starting a *new* conversation in the *same* directory does NOT reload skills.
- The only code path that invalidates the cache is instance dispose/reload, which is not exposed to the user (no `/reload` command, no button in the web UI).

## What would help (any one of these)

- Hot-reload of just the skill/agent cache: a file watcher on skill directories, or a `/reload` command / API endpoint, so a single conversation's instance refreshes without touching the others.
- Or at least a per-directory reload trigger in the web UI (equivalent to the settings-save reload the TUI performs), so I can refresh only the project I'm working on and leave the other conversations running.

This would also enable the workflow where the agent itself develops skills/agents and uses them on the fly in the same session.

**Windows headless `opencode serve` long-run variant — RSS grows to 1-4GB over 1-2 days, then the server wedges (process alive, port listening, HTTP hangs)**

Environment: Windows 11 x64, opencode 1.18.18 (also reproduced on the version from 2026-07), `opencode serve --port 47600 --hostname 127.0.0.1` running 24/7 as a headless engine, driven programmatically by a custom dashboard (our control plane polls the HTTP API every 2s, holds one SSE `/event` consumer per open UI tab, and periodically creates/forks/closes sessions).

Two wedges observed so far (2026-07-12, 2026-08-14), same shape:

1. Fresh boot: ~330MB RSS (with 7 sessions; ~630MB with 229 sessions — session count barely matters).
2. RSS grows steadily over 1-2 days of dashboard restarts and SSE reconnects.
3. Eventually the server **wedges**: process alive, port still listening, but every HTTP request (even `/global/health`) hangs until timeout. Lightweight endpoints hang too. Memory at wedge: 4.2GB (first incident), ~1GB (second, caught earlier).
4. On the dead engine we observed a lingering `CLOSE_WAIT` connection whose remote end (a force-killed dashboard process) no longer existed — matches the zombie-SSE signature from #15645 / #22550.

Our mitigation (works, but treats the symptom): a watchdog recycles the engine via port-pid kill + respawn while it's still healthy-but-bloated, before the wedge. We'd rather not need it.

```text
opencode serve --port 47600
# loop N times:
#   open an SSE connection to /event
#   kill the client process abruptly (no clean close)
#   reconnect a few seconds later
# watch RSS climb and CLOSE_WAIT count accumulate on :47600
```

We have per-2-min telemetry (RSS, thread count, TCP state counts incl. closeWait, session count) from a monitor we ran after the first incident — happy to share the CSV, and we can try to capture a heap snapshot next time it grows past 1GB (the manual ctrl+p flow doesn't apply to a headless serve; if there's a CLI/flag for snapshotting a serve process, point us at it and we'll attach one at the 1GB and wedge points).

Thanks for the detailed report. We reproduced the catalog output from the original configuration, but the permission patterns do not match the configured MCP server names.

OpenCode preserves hyphens when normalizing MCP server and tool names. With servers named `fs-b`, `fs-c`, and `shell-c`, a `ping` tool receives these permission actions:

```text
fs-b_ping
fs-c_ping
shell-c_ping
```

The reported rules use `fs_c_*` and `shell_c_*`, replacing `-` with `_`. Those patterns therefore do not match `fs-c_ping` or `shell-c_ping`, so all three namespaces remain visible.

I tested the shipped `0.0.0-next-17430` Linux binary in an isolated standalone environment with three local Code Mode MCP servers matching the report:

- Using the reported `fs_c_*` and `shell_c_*` deny actions, the catalog contained `fs-b`, `fs-c`, and `shell-c`.
- Changing the actions to `fs-c_*` and `shell-c_*` left only `fs-b` in the catalog.
- A separate two-server control likewise showed both namespaces when allowed and removed the denied namespace when its correctly normalized action was denied.

The corrected V2 rules are:

```json
[
  { "action": "fs-c_*", "resource": "*", "effect": "deny" },
  { "action": "shell-c_*", "resource": "*", "effect": "deny" }
]
```

Characters outside letters, numbers, `_`, and `-` are replaced with `_`; hyphens themselves are preserved. We therefore could not reproduce permissions being ignored when the rules matched the generated action names, so this is being closed as not planned.

Corrected the follow-up in `69d3227b52` after re-checking native compaction semantics.

`tail_start_id` is intentionally absent when a completed compaction summarizes the full history (`SessionCompaction.select` returns no tail when `keep.start === 0`). Treating every missing tail as incomplete made the row walk hydrate history older than a valid completed compaction, defeating the bounded-hydration change and potentially reintroducing context overflow.

The update now:
- stops at completed no-tail compactions in both the iterable and paginated paths
- keeps full history only when the compaction is genuinely incomplete (no completed summary)
- restores the invalid-old-part regression so a completed full compaction proves older parts are not hydrated

Additional environment worth covering: the same stale-mode behavior reproduces when opencode runs inside a terminal multiplexer that caches and replays the host palette (herdr 0.8.0), even on macOS.

Mechanism there: opencode's `system` theme only refreshes on a `\e[?997` color-scheme report or SIGUSR2 (`packages/tui/src/context/theme.tsx` `resolveSystemTheme`/`refreshSystemTheme`). The multiplexer only forwards `?997` when its host terminal emits one, and it additionally answers OSC 10/11/4 queries itself from a cached `host_terminal_theme`. So if the outer terminal doesn't emit `?997` (e.g. Terminal.app), the palette detection result stays cached at first paint and the theme never flips — the multiplexer-side equivalent of the Windows 11 title-bar/background decoupling described here.

This parallels https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/42635 (filed from the same repro inside herdr). A focus-triggered or periodic `getPalette()` re-query would address both.

This is the herdr/multiplexer-specific instance of the same root cause as #36252 (TUI dark/light does not follow host theme), which the bot also linked via #38506/#40023. I've added the multiplexer reproduction detail to #36252 here: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/36252#issuecomment-5296921389

Happy to have this issue closed as a duplicate of #36252 — the actionable scope (refresh palette on focus/periodically so `system` follows the host without a `?997` report) is captured there.
